messages:
maria: quick sync idea 1: propose a low-risk migration path to move controlplane traffic off our big shared VPC into a set of per-region controlplane VPCs. primary goals: reduce blast radius, make audits simpler, and let regions be independently upgraded. thinking PrivateLink read-only mirror for initial validation.

josh: sounds sensible. main concerns: route churn on route-table updates and how we preserve stable egress IPs that customers allowlist. also cost of additional CP VPCs.

devon: PrivateLink mirror is attractive because it avoids full routing changes for the canary. we can expose read-only endpoints that proxy /status, /meta, and read-only APIs to observe traffic without flipping writes.

anika: agree on canary. need to define clear failover semantics: healthchecks, DNS weight thresholds, and whether we fail open (fall back to shared) or fail closed. security wants the default to fail back to shared cp to avoid writes getting dropped.

maria: suggested phased plan:
1) create cp-region-* VPCs and deploy controlplane replicas (read-only)
2) publish PrivateLink interfaces (read-only) and mirror certs/keys with short TTLs
3) run load-replay against private endpoints for 24h to compare latencies and auth behavior
4) enable split-horizon DNS with weighted records (5% -> 25% -> 100%) for read paths
5) after validation, promote some write endpoints and gradually deprecate shared peering

sam: DNS detail: use health-checked weighted A records in Route53 (or simple LB weights) so we can instantly shift weights if metrics regress. document TTLs and expected propagation.

lee: egress IPs: ops recommends pre-allocating NAT IPs for cp-region and mapping them in our allowlist mapping table. otherwise customers will see new source IPs mid-cutover which breaks allowlists. reserve ranges now.

devon: quick cert rotation sketch: store certs in SSM securely and have a rollout worker pull and hot-swap. pseudocode: 

```bash
aws ssm put-parameter --name /redwood/cp/cert/$REGION --type SecureString --value "$(cat cp.pem)" --overwrite
# rollout job fetches param, notifies service, performs hot-swap with zero-downtime handshake
```

anika: monitoring checklist for canary: cp_auth_fail_rate, cp_5xx_rate, nat_snat_mismatch_count, dns_weighted_failovers, route_table_stabilization_secs, write_path_errors. set pages and runbooks before traffic shift.

oncall-bot: Updated paging policy: controlplane-migration -> page if cp_auth_fail_rate > 0.4% sustained for 3m or cp_5xx_rate spike > 1% over 2m.

josh: cross-account KMS/IAM: remember that peered VPCs still require role trusts for decrypting secrets in another account. spike should validate KMS key policies and assume-role flows.

maria: rollback patterns: short TTL DNS, health-checked weighted records, and a circuit-breaker in the routing controller to revert traffic instantly. also an ops playbook to remap egress IPs back if needed.

sam: I'll draft the DNS failover runbook and a play-by-play rollback checklist (including exact Route53 changes and expected propagation windows).

devon: I'll run the PrivateLink read-only spike and collect perf baselines. will also confirm that ip-per-ENI scaling is sufficient for expected canary volume.

josh: I'll build terraform modules for cp-region VPCs, privatelink endpoints, and route automation with idempotent apply + plan gate.

anika: security will review the cert rotation TTLs, KMS policies, and the failback behavior. also request a short threat model for temporary split-state during cutover.

maria: excellent. volunteers: @devon spike, @josh infra/terraform, @sam dns/runbook. I'll write the RFC with exact sequence, Terraform diff, metrics, and rollback SOP and post it here. :thumbsup:
